title: High-AOV jewelry brand cut returns 24% → 9% and doubled Meta ROAS by selling certainty, not the algorithm
content: A Jaipur D2C silver and lab-grown jewelry brand (AOV ₹6,800) was burning ₹20L/month on Meta but barely breaking even. Prospecting ROAS sat at 1.9, and the real leak was a 24% return rate — almost all of it 'looked different in person' and 'unsure buying jewelry online at this price'. After reverse-shipping and restocking, net contribution in tier-2 metros like Lucknow, Indore and Surat was near zero. We fixed buying risk, not targeting. One: a free 5-piece try-at-home box (refundable ₹500 hold via WhatsApp, COD-friendly) shown only to warm retargeting audiences who'd viewed a PDP twice. Two: we killed static carousels for UGC try-on Reels plus a 40-second 'real weight, BIS hallmark, lab-grown certificate' proof video. Three: a WhatsApp flow with a human stylist for sizing, plus a 7-day no-questions return promise pinned on every PDP. Over 90 days: returns fell 24% → 9%, prospecting ROAS rose 1.9 → 3.4, blended ROAS hit 4.1, try-at-home converted at 31%, CAC dropped ₹1,950 → ₹1,280, and net contribution margin moved from ~2% to 21% — on the same ad budget.
lesson: At high AOV the conversion blocker is rarely the creative hook — it's unresolved buying risk. Engineer risk-reversal (try-at-home, proof-of-authenticity video, a human on WhatsApp) before you touch targeting, and the same Meta spend prints double the ROAS while returns collapse. Returns are a trust problem wearing a logistics costume.
